steps.title: A food wine
steps.body: Barbera's high acidity and low tannin make it one of the most food-friendly reds. It suits tomato sauces, pizza, lasagne, salumi, fatty meats and even mushrooms. It cuts through richness without clashing. In Piedmont, it goes with bagna cauda, a warm garlic and anchovy dip.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve at 15 to 17 degrees. Unoaked Barbera is best within three years. Oaked Barbera d'Alba, d'Asti Superiore and Nizza can age five to ten years. Its acidity helps it keep, but fruit fades before structure develops.
steps.highlight: Unoaked young; oaked five to ten years

steps.prompt: Why does Barbera suit tomato-based dishes?
options: Its high acidity matches tomato's acidity

steps.title: Spotting quality
steps.body: Good Barbera balances its acidity with ripe fruit. Overcropped Barbera tastes thin and sour. Lower yields, older vines and good sites give more depth. In the 1980s, producers' new focus turned it from a peasant wine into a respected one.

steps.explanation: Sweet desserts make dry red taste sour.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Barbera's acidity makes it very food-friendly
Unoaked is best young; oaked lasts five to ten years
